items.title: Write execution plan document for missing_scope_check guidance ergonomics
items.context: The plan must distinguish missing scope evidence from missing CLI capability, preserve PLAN gate semantics, keep scope_check_save as reviewer-written signed evidence, and define how Lattice should execute the implementation later.

happy.desc: Draft plan document exists and states that scope_check_save already exists while scope-check.json is the missing PLAN evidence artifact.

edge.desc: Plan explicitly rejects auto-generating scope_check_save evidence or letting the main agent self-sign scope review.

adversarial.desc: Plan cannot claim Authority Server completion, receipt verification, or changed PLAN gate semantics for this documentation story.

verificationEvidence.note: No whitespace errors in the execution plan document diff.
Plan explicitly covers scope_check_save, missing scope-check.json, no self-signing/auto-generation, Authority boundary, and follow-up execution handoff.
Document does not claim implementation or Authority completion; it names future follow-up lifecycle work.

items.title: Run two-host audit of the execution plan
items.context: Use two independent host perspectives to audit only real correctness issues: no arbitrary optimization, no gate weakening, no Authority overclaim, and consistency with Lattice host-neutral CLI/Authority Server boundaries.
items.userSees: User sees "Two-host audit complete: Claude-style host PASS/PENDING and Codex-style host PASS/PENDING with blockers listed".

happy.desc: Two independent host-style audit reports exist and both review the same draft plan artifact.

edge.desc: Audit prompts require no arbitrary optimization, only real correctness issues, and consistency of logic.

adversarial.desc: Audits explicitly check that the plan does not weaken scope_check_save reviewer authority or confuse CLI Non-authority with Authority Server receipt proof.

verificationEvidence.note: Two independent host-style audit reports reviewed the same draft artifact. Both returned BLOCKED on the same real schema issue in the scope_check_save example, with no other blockers.

verificationEvidence.command: Audit prompts for Aquinas and Nietzsche
verificationEvidence.note: Both audit prompts explicitly required no arbitrary optimization, only real correctness issues, and consistency of logic.

items.title: Incorporate audit findings and save final executable document
items.context: Only incorporate real correctness findings. Final doc must include execution steps, verification, rollback, Non-authority vs Authority boundary, and criteria for Lattice execution.
items.userSees: User sees "Final execution plan saved; accepted audit findings incorporated; no unresolved high/critical plan blockers".

happy.desc: Final plan incorporates accepted audit findings and records rejected non-correctness suggestions with rationale.

edge.desc: Final plan includes verification and rollback steps specific to missing_scope_check guidance, not a broad lifecycle rewrite.

adversarial.desc: Final plan preserves scope_check_save as PLAN-only reviewer-written signed evidence and excludes auto-signing or Authority overclaim.

items.title: Hand final document to Lattice execution flow
items.context: After the doc is audited and finalized, identify the exact Lattice story/commands needed to execute it, without claiming implementation is complete until the normal lifecycle reaches DONE.
items.userSees: User sees "Lattice execution handoff ready: follow-up implementation story is proposed, not yet claimed DONE".

happy.desc: Final plan names the follow-up implementation story scope and the Lattice commands needed to execute it.

edge.desc: Execution handoff distinguishes document completion from implementation completion and requires normal lifecycle gates for the follow-up.

adversarial.desc: Execution handoff does not claim that Lattice already changed story_review/session behavior, nor that Authority Server has verified anything.
